R3_motion.criterion: A filter result on the solutions explorer lands at once, with the focus ring as the one animated element.
R3_motion.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when choosing a filter replaces the grid immediately, with no fade, slide or stagger, while a focused control still animates its ring. Answer no when the grid eases, fades or staggers into place.
R3_motion.rationale: The filter result lands immediately without grid animation, while focused controls retain a short animated focus ring. This directly satisfies the positive motion requirement.
evidence: On /solutions, selecting the Output filter value “Hydrogen” changed the result count from “Showing 8 of 8 solutions” to “Showing 2 of 8 solutions” and replaced the eight-card grid with only Transport and Steel.

A CDP motion capture started immediately before that filter selection and stopped after the updated count appeared recorded animation_count=0, directly showing no fade, slide, or stagger during grid replacement.
Computed styles on a resulting grid item showed transition-property:none, transition-duration:0s, animation-name:none, animation-duration:0s, opacity:1, and transform:none.

Separate CDP captures of focusing controls recorded exactly two 120 ms ease-out animations—outline-color and outline-offset—while the focused select had a solid 3px blue outline. Focusing the search field produced the same two outline animations.
A second filter selection (“Multi module”) likewise settled with animation_count=0.

R10_ui_visual.criterion: The fixed top bar carries the logo lockup, the route labels and one Get in Touch action.
R10_ui_visual.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a slim bar across the top of every route holds the stacked-band logo beside the company name, the route labels and a single Get in Touch action. Answer no when the bar is missing one of the three, or when navigation sits in a side rail instead.
R10_ui_visual.rationale: Direct snapshots, route transition, scroll behavior, computed visibility, and measured bounding boxes establish a slim fixed horizontal top bar containing the Zettajoule logo/brand lockup, route labels, and one header Get in Touch action. Navigation is horizontal rather than in a side rail. Although another Get in Touch exists later in the page/footer, the criterion’s singular action is clearly satisfied within the top bar.
evidence: At 1920×1200 on route /, the top-row brand link “Zettajoule” occupied x=370–501, y=13–49; route links ran from “Company” at x=495–568, y=13–49 through “Contact” at x=1156–1230, y=13–49; the sole header “Get in Touch” occupied x=1419–1550, y=12–50. These aligned bounding boxes directly establish a slim horizontal top bar rather than a side rail.

The / snapshot exposed exactly nine header route labels: Company, Technology, Solutions, Our Edge, Our Team, Investors, News, Careers, and Contact, followed by one header Get in Touch action. The brand was identified as class “brand”, aria-label “Zettajoule, home”, href “/”; the action linked to “/contact”.

After scrolling from the top to PageDown and then End, the brand and Get in Touch bounding boxes remained unchanged at y≈12–50 and visible, directly supporting that the bar is fixed/sticky during page scrolling.
Navigation to /company retained the same header contents: Zettajoule, all nine route labels, and one top-bar Get in Touch action, showing the layout persists across the tested route transition.

Supplied deterministic geometry independently records the header wrapper “bar-inner” as display:flex with three horizontal children at x=370, 519, and 1223, plus the route-list ul as display:flex with nine children and the header action link class “get-in-touch”.

R11_functionality.criterion: The first load holds a plain white cover until the reactor is ready to draw.
R11_functionality.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a first visit shows a white cover carrying a progress readout that lifts once the first screen is ready. Answer no when the first screen appears half-drawn, or when the cover lifts before the reactor can render.
R11_functionality.rationale: The browser navigation primitive does not provide a pre-load frame, and the transient cover—if present—had already disappeared by the time each navigation call returned. Therefore I could not directly verify the required white cover, its progress readout, or the ordering between cover removal and the reactor’s first render. Per the evaluation instruction, this missing evidence is not treated as a failure.

Repeated first-visit navigations to / (using fresh query strings) returned only after the completed page was already visible, with the hero text “Powering the World” and the reactor-sequence description present.
Immediate snapshots after navigation showed the full homepage; they did not expose the transient initial loading state.
Direct waits immediately after separate reloads found no visible “Loading”, “%”, or “Preparing” text within 1 second.

Animation capture consistently observed one running 1700 ms infinite pulse animation, but the available evidence does not identify its element or prove that it is a white progress cover that lifts only after reactor readiness.

R12_ux_flow.criterion: Every empty list on the account route states what is absent.
R12_ux_flow.evaluation_rule: Answer yes when an account with no saves, no searches and no applications sees a message on each list naming what is missing and offering a way onward. Answer no when an empty list renders as blank space.
R12_ux_flow.rationale: The required account state—no saves, no searches, and no applications—was directly established and verified after reload. Every empty list explicitly names what is absent and provides a clear route onward; none renders as blank space.
evidence: On the authenticated /account route, after removing the final saved solution through its confirmation dialog, the persisted zero state read: “Saved solutions 0”, “Nothing saved yet”, “Save a card in the explorer and it lands here.” and offered the “Open the explorer” link.

After removing the final saved search through its confirmation dialog, the persisted zero state read: “Saved searches 0”, “No saved search”, “Filter the explorer and save that combination under a name.” and offered the “Go and filter” link.

The account already had no applications, and its empty state read: “Job applications 0”, “No application sent”, “Apply to an open job and it appears here with its status.” and offered the “See open jobs” link.
A direct reload of /account preserved all three zero states and their explanatory onward links, confirming these were rendered account states rather than transient notices.
